title: Re-pitch: samples land in key
thisBuild: Sample sheet, Play tab: a Re-pitch key. A sound with one clear note (a pluck, a hum, a bass hit) moves so that note is a C, so keys, chords and the Roll play the notes they say. A melody or loop moves into the mess's key by the fewest steps and keeps its length.
It takes out the sound's own tuning drift too, so a sample a little sharp or flat lands on the note.
Works on sounds as short as a tenth of a second. A line under the key says what it heard and how far it moved it. Undo puts it back; Tune and Fine stay yours.
Settings, Playing: Auto-pitch new sounds. Every new mic take, import or sound you put on a pad is re-pitched by itself, and loops moved by their key follow the mess when you change its key.
watch: Sample something melodic, tap Re-pitch, and play it on the keys: do the notes match the key names?
Try a loop, then change the mess's key with Auto-pitch on: does it follow?
Tell me about any sound it reads wrong (the line under Re-pitch shows what it heard).
limits: Drums and noise have no note, so they stay as they are.
A tapped one-shot plays its C. Play it from the keys to hear other notes.
Moves are never more than 6 semitones, so a far-off sound can still change character a little.
